data.label: Background
data.note: Drifts sideways while it zooms in and out.

data.label: Disc
data.note: Circles the centre, turning about its own.

data.label: Bright parts
data.note: Half the size is enough for what's blurred.

data.label: Start here
data.note:
View 0 shows every tile; 1 to 9 shows one whole. Scrub the numbers: none of them recompiles.

Dotted links carry values that are the same for the whole frame. Only those can set sizes, counts and times: try linking a UV to a Render Texture's scale, and hover the red link.

Every group here is yours to enter (Enter) and edit.

data.label: 1 · Picture
data.note: A Render Texture draws a value into a texture of its own: here a scale of the canvas, a frame value that follows View. The other tiles read it instead of drawing the picture again.

data.label: 2 · Optical Flow
data.note: Previous Frame keeps the last frame in a simulation; Optical Flow estimates how far each pixel moved since, coarse to fine, in Repeat Passes zones (enter it). Hue is the direction, saturation the speed.

data.label: 3 · Motion Arrows
data.note: The flow at the centre of each cell, per second like the colours, and longer than it is so it can be seen.

data.label: 4 · Flow Error
data.note: What's left between this frame and the previous one carried by the flow, 8 times brighter: black where the estimate is right. The disc's edge uncovers pixels nothing can predict.

data.label: 5 · Datamosh
data.note: A Simulation zone: its image is moved along the flow instead of redrawn, so the picture smears. A new picture fades in slowly, and the whole of it is let in again every 4 seconds.

data.label: 6 · Mip levels
data.note: A Render Texture with mips on also keeps smaller and smaller copies of itself. Sample Texture reads any level, and between two: here one that comes and goes with Time.

data.label: 7 · Glow
data.note: A Repeat Passes zone (enter Glow): whole passes repeated as many times as a value says, here one that changes with Time. Each pass knows its iteration, and reads farther than the last.

data.label: 8 · Pixelate by Halves
data.note: A Repeat Passes zone whose texture is half the size in each iteration. The result is read with the Closest filter, so its texels show.

data.label: 9 · Exact texels
data.note: A picture drawn at 64×36 pixels whatever the canvas, then read texel by texel with Load Texel.

data.label: Tiles
data.note: One Render Texture draws several values at once, as many to a pass as WebGPU lets it. Linked straight to a Texture input, each would be drawn by itself, at the canvas' size.
